evidence.snippet: In five patients from four unrelated families, we identified biallelic variants in HMGCS1 (3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A synthase).

evidence.reference_title: HMGCS1 variants cause rigid spine syndrome amenable to mevalonic acid treatment in an animal model.
evidence.snippet: Hmgcs1 mutant zebrafish displayed severe early defects, including immobility at 2 days and death by Day 3 post-fertilisation and were rescued by HMGCS1 mRNA.

nodes.description: Six missense variants and one frameshift variant are distributed across HMGCS1. Four missense proteins (p.Q29L, p.M70T, p.C268S, p.S447P) remain dimeric; three are less thermostable and two show subtle changes in enzymatic activity. All four rescue hmgcs1 mutant zebrafish less well than wild-type HMGCS1 mRNA, so the missense alleles retain partial function rather than abolishing it.

nodes.description: HMG-CoA formed by HMGCS1 is reduced by HMGCR to mevalonate, which feeds both isoprenoid and cholesterol synthesis. Loss of HMGCS1 activity limits both branches; which product deficit drives the muscle disease has not been determined. In zebrafish, mevalonic acid bypasses the defective step and lessens mutant severity.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl CoA synthase I reveals requirements for isoprenoid and cholesterol synthesis in oligodendrocyte migration arrest, axon wrapping, and myelin gene expression.
evidence.snippet: Through a forward genetic screen in zebrafish we discovered that mutation of hmgcs1, which encodes an enzyme necessary for isoprenoid and cholesterol synthesis, causes oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) to migrate past their target axons and to fail to express myelin genes.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the zebrafish hmgcs1 gene reveal a novel function for isoprenoids during red blood cell development.
evidence.snippet: hmgcs1 encodes the first enzyme in the cholesterol synthesis pathway and mutation of hmgcs1 inhibits cholesterol synthesis.
